international.title: Plant-based lunches could cut Australia’s emissions by 15m tonnes, new research shows
international.summary: Nationwide change in lunch habits could cut more climate pollution than grounding every domestic flight Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australians could collectively cut climate pollution by more than 15m tonnes – more than grounding every domestic flight – simply by changing what they eat for lunch. A nationwide shift to plant-based lunches could reduce food-related emissions by 29% – 15.4m tonnes per year – while saving the average household about $611 annually, according to a report by Bryant Research and not-for-profit ProVeg.
